name: The Amalekite who claimed to kill Saul
charge: Claiming to have slain the Lord’s anointed, and bringing his crown for a reward
summary: A young man came out of the camp of Israel to Ziklag with his clothes rent and earth upon his head, and fell before David with the crown and the bracelet of Saul: he said he had come by chance upon mount Gilboa, found Saul leaning on his spear, and slew him at his own asking. The earlier chapter says Saul fell on his own sword. He was an Amalekite, of the seed of Esau, the nation written of as fearing not God, and he expected a reward for the deed. His own mouth testified against him, and David had him slain.
offenseFull: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and abode two days in Ziklag, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent and earth upon his head and fell to the earth before David. He said the people were fled from the battle, many were fallen and dead, and Saul and Jonathan his son were dead also. Asked how he knew it, he said he happened by chance upon mount Gilboa and found Saul leaning upon his spear with the chariots and horsemen following hard after him; Saul asked who he was, and he answered that he was an Amalekite; then Saul asked him to stand upon him and slay him, because anguish was come upon him while his life was yet whole in him, so he stood upon him and slew him, being sure he could not live after he was fallen, and took the crown from his head and the bracelet from his arm and brought them to his lord (2 Samuel 1:2-10). The earlier account says Saul took a sword and fell upon it (1 Samuel 31:3-5). The man was an Amalekite: Amalek came of Eliphaz the son of Esau (Genesis 36:12). He carried the crown and the bracelet as tokens of a deed he expected to be paid for.

David took hold on his clothes and rent them, and so did all the men with him, and they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan his son, and for the house of Israel, because they were fallen by the sword. The renting of garments was the sign of mourning, but the Most High looks for a rent heart and not rent garments only, for true repentance is inward (Joel 2:13). The opening of the throne was no occasion for celebration, and the man who brought the crown had misjudged the king he brought it to.
judgmentFull: David asked the young man where he was from, and he answered that he was the son of a stranger, an Amalekite. Then David asked how he was not afraid to stretch forth his hand to destroy the Lord’s anointed (2 Samuel 1:13-16). The answer to that question is written in the law: Amalek met Israel by the way, smote the hindmost when they were faint and weary, and he feared not God (Deuteronomy 25:18). That nation has had a perpetual hatred and has shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity (Ezekiel 35:5), pursuing his brother with the sword, casting off all pity, and keeping his wrath for ever (Amos 1:11). The man who had twice refused to put forth his hand against Saul, saying the Lord forbid it (1 Samuel 26:11), was not going to reward a stranger for claiming the act. David called one of his young men and told him to go near and fall upon him, and he smote him that he died; his blood was upon his own head, for his own mouth had testified against him. Whether or not he had done what he claimed, his mouth condemned him; he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword (Revelation 13:10). David remembered this messenger when Rechab and Baanah brought him the head of Ish-bosheth: the man who thought he brought good tidings of Saul was taken hold of and slain in Ziklag, and that was the reward he got for his tidings (2 Samuel 4:10).

Then David lamented over Saul and over Jonathan, and bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow, which is written in the book of Jasher (2 Samuel 1:17-18). The book of Jasher is not in the canon because the Most High did not will us to have it; He put in the book exactly what His people need in the last days. And this walk is not by the bow nor by

the gun: not by might, nor by power, but by His spirit (Zechariah 4:6); here is the patience of the saints, they that keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus (Revelation 14:12). There is nothing wrong with knowing how to defend yourself, but the redemption of Israel does not come by force of arms. The lament itself is prophecy given in the spirit: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided, swifter than eagles and stronger than lions (2 Samuel 1:23). Before the devil jumped on Saul he was a good man, and the forefathers died only when the Most High said it was time; the man who boasted of hastening it lost his own life for it.

lawsResolved.text: Those guilty of murder are to be put to death.
We should respect and give obedience to rulers and authorities who preside as God's ministers.
You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.
Acquiring treasures by lying is the fleeting fantasy of those who seek death.

text.text: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?
And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.
And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.

So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers.

Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.
And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek: these were the sons of Adah Esau’s wife.
And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the Lord’s anointed?
And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the Lord’s anointed.
How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.
Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever:
The Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.
He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.
When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who thought that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:
And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:
(Also he bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.)
Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.
Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.
Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.
